title: Wine Scoring
body: Wine quality reflects several stages of its making: the vineyard, pressing, fermentation, ageing and storage. A strong harvest is a useful foundation, but later handling still contributes to the result.
The Almanac's bottle report shows the actual quality score and its contribution breakdown. Scores are kept within the displayed quality scale; improving one stage does not promise an unlimited total.

Ageing treatments have different contributions and wine-style trade-offs. Their quality penalties are part of those choices, not a promise that an otherwise identical batch will randomly spoil. Choose a vessel for its role and inspect the result.

Quality, tasting character, readiness and appraisal answer different questions. Market guidance is an estimate, not a guaranteed offer from every merchant. Use the live wine report and the merchant's actual offer when deciding whether to keep, serve or sell a bottle.
